title: Cladone gateway configuration (api-routes.json)
description: Formal grammar of the Gate One configuration file. Complementary source of truth: gate-one-src/internal/core/routes.go (JSON tags). Only implemented fields are described — any unknown field is rejected by the strict test (core: TestLoadRealConfigStrict).

$schema.description: Optional reference to this schema (autocompletion and validation in the editor).

securityHeaders.description: Platform-wide response hardening, emitted by the gateway on EVERY response it serves (proxied or generated: health, stats, 401/403, MCP metadata, PWA assets, CSP collector). Declaring the block applies the secure defaults; each field can be tightened or disabled. Referrer-Policy is only set when the response does not already carry one (a proxified app's stricter policy wins). Absent = nothing (an install whose edge proxy already sets them can opt out).

hstsMaxAge.description: Strict-Transport-Security max-age, in seconds. Absent = 15552000 (180 days); 0 = header omitted (e.g. a host that must stay reachable in plain HTTP). Keep includeSubDomains/preload off until every subdomain is HTTPS-only: with preload the choice becomes permanent in browsers.

hstsPreload.description: Append preload. Requires hstsIncludeSubDomains (refused at load otherwise). Default false.

referrerPolicy.description: Referrer-Policy value. Absent = strict-origin-when-cross-origin; empty string = header omitted.

license.description: Optional offline signed licence (Ed25519). Absent, invalid or expired = evaluation/personal mode: the gateway keeps serving; the user badge shows a notice. The private signing key NEVER ships (only publicKey is embedded).

tokenFile.description: Path to a file holding the token (mounted secret, easy renewal: replace the file + SIGHUP). Overridden by GATE_ONE_LICENSE_TOKEN; falls back to `token` when unreadable.

publicKey.description: Ed25519 public key, base64 (raw 32 bytes). Public by design, safe to commit. Legacy single-key form (tokens without kid).

publicKeys.description: kid → Ed25519 public key (base64). Several keys can be valid at once during a rotation; tokens carry their signed kid. An unknown kid is rejected.

url.description: Registration/pricing URL shown by the badge.

authProvider.description: Authentication provider. `dev` is the embedded loopback-only IdP used for onboarding/tests; `http` is any external service implementing the Gate One auth contract (auth-bridge is the reference implementation; a non-conforming service needs an adapter); `oidc` is the native Relying Party (discovery, code+PKCE, JWKS, session, logout, MCP resource server). Absent = legacy oidc + auth-bridge translation, so existing configs are unchanged.

type.description: Provider implementation. Default: dev when a dev block is present, oidc when clientId is present, jwt when jwksUrl is present, http otherwise.

id.description: Unique provider id when declared in authProviders. The legacy authProvider block is normalized to id "default".

cookieName.description: Session cookie name for type oidc. Empty = gate_one_session for the default provider, a provider-scoped name for additional providers.

baseUrl.description: Service root for type http (default http://auth-bridge:3000, or AUTH_BRIDGE_URL).

loginBaseUrl.description: Public origin of the login service. For dev it hosts the embedded login page, e.g. http://login.demo.localhost:3000 (no path/query).

loginUrl.description: Full login page URL. Defaults to loginBaseUrl + /login, then (type http) the legacy oidc.loginUrl, then baseUrl + /login.

issuer.description: OIDC issuer advertised in MCP protected-resource metadata. Defaults to the legacy oidc.issuer, or loginBaseUrl + /dev for dev.

cookieDomain.description: Shared parent domain of the session cookie (dev), e.g. demo.localhost. Required for dev.

verifyUrl.description: Identity verification endpoint (type http). Default baseUrl + /auth.

mcpVerifyUrl.description: MCP bearer verification endpoint (type http). Default baseUrl + /auth/mcp.

headers.description: Maps the identity response headers of an external provider (type http). Empty = auth-bridge defaults.

clientId.description: OIDC client ID (type oidc). The client must be registered at the IdP with the redirect URI below.

clientSecretEnv.description: Environment variable holding the OIDC client secret (type oidc). Absent/empty = public client (PKCE only). Never put the secret in this file.

scopes.description: OIDC scopes. Default: openid, profile, email.

redirectUrl.description: OIDC callback URL registered at the IdP. Default: loginBaseUrl + /auth/callback.

roleClaims.description: Dot paths into the ID token claims mapped to roles. Default: realm_access.roles, resource_access.<clientId>.roles, groups.

scopesClaim.description: Claim holding the granted scopes (default scope; scp is always also read).

mcpAudience.description: MCP access-token audience policy. Empty = scope-only (compatible default). A literal value requires that value in aud. "auto" requires the endpoint's own protected-resource identifier (recommended, and used with Keycloak audience mappers).

jwksUrl.description: JWKS endpoint for type jwt. Required for jwt; the provider never hosts a login page.

audience.description: Expected audience for type jwt (empty = no audience check, or the MCP resource when VerifyMCP is used).

algorithms.description: Allowed JWT algorithms for type jwt. Default [EdDSA].

header.description: Bearer header name for type jwt. Default Authorization.

cacheTtlSeconds.description: JWKS cache TTL for type jwt. Default 300.

sessionTtlSeconds.description: OIDC RP session lifetime. Default 3600 (1h): a short TTL bounds revocation when no shared store is used. The refresh/reauth flow renews it.

links.description: Links owned by the authentication connector, displayed in the user badge. account is the IdP's own account console: NO OIDC standard, so the URL is explicit (Keycloak /realms/<realm>/account/, Entra myaccount.microsoft.com, Google myaccount.google.com, Okta /enduser/settings…).

sessionKeyEnv.description: Environment variable holding the RP cookie signing key (base64/random string, hashed to 32 bytes). Empty = the key is generated and persisted in the bbolt store. Required for multi-instance (shared key).

sessionStore.description: RP-side revocation store (back-channel logout, RP logout). Default: bbolt at ./gate-one-state.db, relative to the config file. bbolt is single-writer: a second Gate One instance on the same file is refused. Redis is the shared, multi-instance backend and makes revocation visible on the next request on every instance.

type.description: bolt (default, single instance) or redis (shared, multi-instance, immediate revocation).

path.description: bbolt file path. Default ./gate-one-state.db (relative to the config file).

url.description: Redis URL for type redis (redis:// or rediss://). Mutually exclusive with sentinel mode.

masterName.description: Redis Sentinel master name. Requires sentinelAddrs.

passwordEnv.description: Environment variable holding the Redis password. Never put the password in this file.

prefix.description: Shared revocation key prefix. Default cladone:auth:v1:. Must match the broker's redis.authPrefix.

dialTimeoutMs.description: Redis dial timeout in milliseconds. Default 500.

readTimeoutMs.description: Redis read timeout in milliseconds. Default 300.

writeTimeoutMs.description: Redis write timeout in milliseconds. Default 300.

backchannelLogout.description: OIDC Back-Channel Logout. Absent = auto: enabled when the IdP discovery advertises backchannel_logout_supported. false disables it. Register <loginBaseUrl>/backchannel-logout at the IdP.

legacyTokenCookies.description: Migration bridge: also set auth-bridge's access_token/refresh_token/id_token cookies on cookieDomain, so auth-bridge's token-broker proxy routes (/connections, /connect, /oauth) resolve the same session when both share the login host. Default false. The native session cookie remains authoritative for Gate One.

backchannelForwardUrl.description: Migration bridge: after a valid local back-channel revocation, POST the same logout_token to this auth-bridge /backchannel-logout URL so its persistent sid list stays in sync for /auth and /connections. Best effort.

revocationTtlSeconds.description: Retention of revocation entries. Default: the issuer's advertised refresh-token TTL (cladone_refresh_token_ttl_seconds, e.g. the broker), else 30 days; never shorter than the session TTL. Must cover the refresh-token lifetime for a global logout.

dev.description: Embedded development IdP. Loopback-only; never production.

users.description: Development accounts. Empty = alice/alice (user) and bob/bob (admin). Passwords are plaintext by design (dev only).

mcpToken.description: Bearer accepted by MCP routes. Default dev-<username>.

authProviders.description: Named authentication providers for per-route binding. Mutually exclusive with the legacy singular authProvider. Each item uses the same fields as authProvider plus id/cookieName; a route selects one with auth.provider.

defaultAuthProvider.description: Provider id used by routes that do not set auth.provider. Required when more than one authProviders entry is declared.

defaultAppUrl.description: Absolute http(s) URL where a bare visit to the login host root is redirected (302), preserving the query string. Email verification links (Firebase mode=verifyEmail&oobCode, Keycloak account links) land on https://login.<domain>/ and must reach the application that handles the code. Absent = the login host root stays 404.

oidc.description: LEGACY platform IdP block. When authProvider is absent, it is translated into an http provider (auth-bridge) at load; existing configs keep working. New configurations should use authProvider.

loginUrl.description: Platform login page (e.g. "https://login.example.com/login"). Used by the server-side redirect of frontend routes and by the guard script (per-route authGuard.loginUrl takes precedence).

issuer.description: OIDC issuer (e.g. "https://auth.example.com/realms/example") — announced as the authorization_server of the MCP OAuth metadata.

tokenBroker.description: Internal per-user credential broker. Required only when a route declares upstream.delegated. The shared secret is read from the named environment variable at load (never from this file) and is never logged.

url.description: Broker base URL (default http://token-broker:4000, the Docker internal service name). Never expose it through Traefik.

secretEnv.description: Environment variable holding the X-Broker-Secret shared secret (default TOKEN_BROKER_SHARED_SECRET).

links.description: Links owned by the token broker, displayed in the user badge. services is the connections page (auth-bridge proxies it today): it is rendered only when an exposed route declares upstream.delegated (computed by the gateway).

mcpDefaults.description: Optional defaults shared by every MCP access unit.

scope.description: Default MCP scope when a service/set declares none.

mcpSets.description: Named groups of MCP services exposed with their own access rights (resource/scope/identity) and per-member tool filters. A member endpoint is set.host + set.endpoint + member.path.

userLink.description: A link rendered in the expanded user badge. URL: http(s) absolute or a local absolute path (/...); javascript:/data: are refused. target defaults to _blank; rel is forced to noopener noreferrer.

label.description: Displayed text. Optional for the connector links (default Account/Services); required for userBadge.links.

url.description: http(s) absolute URL or local absolute path (/...).

match.description: Rate-limit / quota triggering conditions (rateLimit.when, quota.when). Two families: technical (method/query/header/body — evaluated BEFORE authentication) and identity (roles/scopes/claims/user — evaluated AFTER authentication on the verified token). All conditions combine with AND. NB: the authentication policy (auth) does NOT use this type: auth.when takes technical conditions only, auth.identity takes identity conditions only.

header.description: Exact equality of headers. Caution: a header is forgeable by the client — never put an authorization there (use roles instead).

body.description: Exact equality of fields of the parsed JSON body (flattened one level).

roles.description: Required Keycloak roles (realm roles + flattened client roles, see auth-bridge's X-Roles). AND between them. Example of a fixed name: offline_access (realm role granted to every user via default-roles-<realm>).

scopes.description: Required granted scopes (token `scope` claim, see auth-bridge's X-Scopes). AND between them. Example of a fixed name: profile (default client scope, always present).

claims.description: Token claims: value "*" = mere presence, otherwise comparison of the stringified value (JSON boolean → "true"/"false", numbers → Go format). AND between them. NB: client_credentials tokens (service accounts) have neither email nor profile claims.

technicalMatch.description: Technical policy conditions, evaluated BEFORE authentication: they decide WHETHER authentication is required (the only family allowed in auth.when). All conditions of one object combine with AND.

header.description: Exact equality of headers. Caution: a header is forgeable by the client — never put an authorization there (use roles instead).

body.description: Exact equality of fields of the parsed JSON body (flattened one level).

identityMatch.description: Identity policy conditions, evaluated AFTER authentication on the verified token (failure = 403 forbidden). All conditions combine with AND.

roles.description: Required Keycloak roles (realm roles + flattened client roles, see auth-bridge's X-Roles). AND between them. Example of a fixed name: offline_access (realm role granted to every user via default-roles-<realm>).

scopes.description: Required granted scopes (token `scope` claim, see auth-bridge's X-Scopes). AND between them. Example of a fixed name: profile (default client scope, always present).

claims.description: Token claims: value "*" = mere presence, otherwise comparison of the stringified value (JSON boolean → "true"/"false", numbers → Go format). AND between them. NB: client_credentials tokens (service accounts) have neither email nor profile claims.

authPolicy.description: Authentication policy. Empty ({}) = authentication ALWAYS required. auth.when holds TECHNICAL conditions (method/query/header/body) deciding when authentication is required: one object (AND of its conditions) or an array (OR of ANDs — required if ANY element matches); absent/empty = always required. auth.identity holds IDENTITY conditions (roles/scopes/claims/user), checked after successful authentication (403 otherwise) and only on requests that were actually authenticated.

provider.description: ID of the authProviders entry used to verify this route. Empty = defaultAuthProvider. The binding is static and compiled at load; a request cannot choose another provider.

userBadgePolicy.description: User badge injected by the guard script once authenticated: collapsed on the top edge (one line = username), expanded on hover/keyboard focus — chosen claims + logout button (OIDC end_session + cookie clearing). Absent = no badge.

claims.description: What the expanded badge displays as claims: true = every claim of the session, false = none, a list = only these (missing ones omitted).

roles.description: Session roles displayed as chips in the expanded badge: true = every role, false = none, a list = only these (same data as the auth.identity.roles conditions, served by the /__gate-one/auth probe).

scopes.description: Granted scopes displayed as chips in the expanded badge: true = every scope, false = none, a list = only these.

logoutLabel.description: Label of the logout button (default Log out).

links.description: Application-specific links, appended after the connector links (account, then services when the deployment delegates). Duplicate URLs are dropped (the connector link wins); at most 8 links after merge.

loginBadge.description: true = the badge ALSO appears when anonymous, from the very first visit, in invitation mode ("👤 Sign in") — clicked, it opens the login tab: offer sign-in without touching the site's markup. Default false (badge only once authenticated; when anonymous it only appears after a detected session death).

uiGateRule.description: UI gating rule by config — for fronts whose markup cannot be modified (if you control the HTML, prefer the data-gtw-* attributes). The selected element is visible only if the session satisfies the conditions (OR on roles, OR on scopes, AND on claims). PRECEDENCE: an element carrying at least one data-gtw-* attribute ignores uiGate rules; several rules on a same element combine with AND; invalid selector = rule ignored.

selector.description: CSS selector (querySelectorAll) of the targeted elements.

roles.description: Visible if AT LEAST ONE of these roles is held.

scopes.description: Visible if AT LEAST ONE of these scopes is granted.

auth.description: Turns the selected elements into login triggers: after = native action preserved + invitation tab; before = click neutralized + direct tab. Activation only: deactivations (unchecking, closing details, reset, returning a value control to its OFF value) are never gated. Value controls (select/range/date/…) are gated on change, with their default value as the OFF value (data-gtw-auth-off on the element overrides it).

hidden.description: Hiding: before = hidden before authentication (any click reaching it is neutralized → banner); after = hidden once authenticated.

rateLimitPolicy.description: Rate limiting: fixed window per identity (authenticated user, else real IP via X-Forwarded-For), per route. Full window = 429 + Retry-After (seconds). Periods: second|minute|hour|day.

quotaPolicy.description: Cumulative quota: same mechanics as rateLimit with a longer window in practice (day). Full window = 429 + Retry-After.

authGuardPolicy.description: 401 guard script (login without reloading: tab + replay + banner + declarative gating). Active by default on frontend routes; no-op elsewhere. The guard intercepts the 401 (login) and, when authGuard.forbidden.banner is set, the gateway's OWN identity 403; a 403 coming from the backend is never concerned.

enabled.description: false = opt-out (the front handles its own 401).

authGuardForbiddenPolicy.description: Opt-in UX for the gateway's OWN identity 403 (rights refusal — auth.identity not satisfied). A backend 403 is never concerned. Browser navigations get a readable HTML page (or a redirect to pageUrl); fetch()/XHR get the JSON 403 unchanged, plus an optional dismissable banner hinting the front authors to hide the feature.

banner.description: true = the injected guard script shows a dismissable banner when a fetch() sees the gateway's identity 403. Default false.

pageUrl.description: Browser navigations refused on identity are redirected there (302) instead of the built-in HTML page.

message.description: Overrides the built-in forbidden page's message text.

url.description: OpenAPI 3.x JSON document of the host (absolute URL, or path relative to the route backend). Also the document used to resolve the mcp policy's operations.

public.description: false = the openapi.json is only served authenticated.

name.description: Tool name exposed to MCP clients (unique per route).

operationId.description: operationId resolved in the host's OpenAPI document; the tool method, path, parameters and body schema are derived from it. An unresolved operationId refuses the configuration load.

name.description: Service name, referenced by mcpSets members. Empty = the route cannot be a set member.

standalone.description: Expose this service on its own endpoint (default true). false = served only through the mcpSets referencing it (the set carries the access rights).

resource.description: OAuth protected-resource identifier (audience) of the standalone service. Empty = the endpoint URL. Ignored when the service is reached through a set.

scope.description: Keycloak client scope required from MCP clients (bearer `scope` claim), announced in /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and checked by auth-bridge (internal X-MCP-Scope header). The realm must grant it. Default: mcp-tools.

operations.description: REST operations exposed as MCP tools. Empty = no tool (the MCP endpoint still serves metadata and initialization). Mutually exclusive with upstream.

mcpSet.description: An MCP access unit grouping services under one endpoint; carries the audience (resource), scope and identity of the group.

endpoint.description: Mount path of the set on that host ("/" allowed).

resource.description: OAuth protected-resource identifier (audience) of the set. Empty = the set endpoint URL.

scope.description: MCP scope required from clients of this set. Default: mcpDefaults.scope, else mcp-tools.

enabled.description: Expose the set (default true). false = the whole set is skipped (no endpoint, no validation).

mcpSetMember.description: One service mounted under a set.

path.description: Path relative to the set endpoint ("/" = the set endpoint itself).

tools.description: Optional glob allow-list restricting the service's tools inside this set.

enabled.description: Expose this member (default true). false = not materialized, and its service is neither compiled (no OpenAPI fetch) nor provider-validated.

mcpUpstreamPolicy.description: Proxy an external MCP server over Streamable HTTP instead of deriving local REST tools. The upstream receives the per-user token of upstream.delegated (or static upstream.headers), never the Gate One bearer. Tool filtering is enforced on both tools/list and tools/call.

url.description: Full upstream Streamable HTTP endpoint. Default: the route backend. The incoming /mcp path is not appended automatically.

mcpToolFilter.description: Glob patterns (path.Match syntax) over MCP tool names. Include non-empty = only matching tools are exposed; Exclude always wins. Hidden tools are also refused on tools/call.

method.description: POST (default) = network-first offline replay of POST/SSE; GET = SWR cache of this exact path; none = full opt-out (never cached, excluded from the apiGETCache catch-all).

maxEntrySizeBytes.description: Default 2 MiB — beyond, streamed but not cached.

version.description: Semantic invalidation of the endpoint's cache (bump it when the backend result changes).

idleFinalizeMs.description: Default 1500 — finalizes the cached response after this SSE silence.

networkTimeoutSeconds.description: Default 3 — network delay before the cache fallback (headers only).

offlineFastPath.description: Default true: offline, serves the cache directly. false = the network failure (bounded by networkTimeoutSeconds) triggers the fallback — for endpoints where replaying a write would be wrong.

pwaApiGETCache.description: Its presence activates the universal GET cache (everything nothing else covers).

excludes.description: Path prefixes never cached by the catch-all.

excludePatterns.description: JS regexes (full URL) never cached — invalid syntax rejected at load.

pwaNetworkOnly.description: Its presence activates the "never cached" route (auth exchanges, OAuth callbacks carrying a one-time code…).

excludePatterns.description: JS regexes (full URL) → straight to the network, no cache.

pwaAssets.description: Strategy of same-origin pages/assets (documents, scripts, styles). Default: staleWhileRevalidate without timeout.

icons.description: Same-host paths referenced by the manifest (Chrome: 192×192 and 512×512 PNG for full install).

upstreamResponseHeaders.description: Adjustment of the backend's RESPONSE headers before sending to the browser — typically remove an origin Content-Security-Policy that would block the injected guard script, or set a deployment header. Prefer csp.merge (hashes) or csp.own (explicit removal, logged) for CSP: removing the origin's CSP here is a blunt, unlogged operation and loses the origin's protections.

set.description: Headers added/overwritten on the response; values with ${VAR} interpolation (container environment); empty value = header removed (never transmitted empty).

remove.description: Header names removed from the response (e.g. Content-Security-Policy).

cspPolicy.description: Content-Security-Policy emitted (or amended) by the gateway — the only component able to generate a per-response nonce and write it into the HTML it already rewrites (guard, PWA, custom injections). By default the origin's policy is NEVER removed or weakened: the gateway's policy is added as a SECOND header (browsers enforce all of them, so the effective rule is the strictest) and the hashes of the gateway's own injected script and guard stylesheet are APPENDED to the origin's script-src / style-src (script-src-elem > script-src > default-src, style-src-elem > style-src > default-src). Set own=true to remove the origin policy explicitly and let the gateway own it (opt-in, logged, requires mode nonce/hash and reportOnly=false). Applied to HTML responses only.

mode.description: "off" = nothing (the origin's policy passes as-is); "merge" = keep the origin policy and only add the hashes of the gateway's injected scripts (no policy of our own); "hash" = emit our policy with those hashes, no body rewrite; "nonce" = emit our policy with a per-response nonce and stamp the HTML in STREAMING mode (O(1) memory, upstream forced to gzip so the body is plain text).

reportOnly.description: Emit Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only instead of the enforcing header (progressive rollout: violations are collected, nothing is blocked). Requires mode nonce or hash.

own.description: The gateway OWNS the policy: the origin's enforced and report-only CSP headers are removed before ours is emitted. Opt-in and logged (never silent). Requires mode nonce or hash and reportOnly=false: removing the origin's enforcing policy to replace it with a report-only one would remove protection without enforcing anything. Use only for a site you control/accept, with a complete policy.

reportTo.description: Local path served by the gateway collecting the violations (report-uri). Default: /__gate-one_csp/report. Bounded ring buffer (256 entries), 16 KiB body limit, 50 reports/second, never authenticated.

stampScripts.description: "inline" (default) = only <script> tags WITHOUT src receive the nonce (external scripts stay governed by the host allow-list); "all" = every <script> tag. Nonce mode only. A tag that already carries a nonce is never rewritten.

directives.description: Directive name → sources, as one string ("'self' https://x") or an array. The gateway appends the nonce (nonce mode) and the injected scripts' / guard stylesheet's hashes to the effective script-src / style-src, and report-uri when reportTo is set. To let the guard's nonce/hash pass, declare style-src (e.g. "'self'").

upstreamPolicy.description: Join to a backend outside the internal network (proxified external site — e.g. Cloudflare Pages/Workers). Absent = unchanged historical behavior: public Host preserved, client headers passed as-is.

host.description: true = the Host header sent to the backend is that of the backend's origin (required for an external site that routes by Host, e.g. Cloudflare — otherwise the request arrives with the public host and the origin does not recognize it). Absent/false = public Host passed as-is (internal backends). TLS/SNI always targets the backend's origin.

hostOverride.description: Explicit value of the Host header sent to the backend, when it must differ from both the public host and the backend's origin (rare). Precedence over host.

headers.description: Static request headers set toward the backend (Set: overwrite any value the client may have sent). Uses: get through an origin basic auth ("Authorization": "Basic ${MYSITE_BASIC_AUTH}") or the Cloudflare Access service tokens (CF-Access-Client-Id / CF-Access-Client-Secret). Values with ${VAR} interpolation from the container environment — missing variable = fatal error at load (never a silent empty credential); empty value = header removed from the request. Values are never logged.

rewriteRedirects.description: true = ABSOLUTE Locations targeting the backend's origin are rewritten to the public host (https scheme, path/query preserved) — otherwise the browser would leave the proxy at the target site's first absolute redirect (e.g. 301 of the trailing slash). Relative Locations and those targeting other origins (e.g. a Cloudflare Access team domain) pass intact. Default: false.

stripCookies.description: REQUEST-side cookie filtering toward the backend. The gateway session cookies (access_token, refresh_token, id_token, session) carry Domain=<parent domain> (COOKIE_DOMAIN, e.g. .cladone.com): the browser presents them to EVERY public host, so without this filter a proxified third-party site receives the user's tokens on every request. "all" = every cookie removed except the names in keep (the proxified app's own cookies); "none" = historical behavior, everything forwarded. Default: "all" as soon as an upstream policy is declared (fail-closed).

keep.description: Cookie names preserved when stripCookies is "all" (typically the proxified application's own session). Names reserved for the gateway session (access_token, refresh_token, id_token, session) are refused at load: they must never reach an external origin.

delegatedCredentialPolicy.description: Per-user credentials supplied by the token broker for the authenticated caller. Requires route.auth (the broker needs an authenticated user id). A missing connection produces a 401/409 with a connect_url (or a redirect for frontend routes), never a request without credentials. The same policy applies to REST tool calls produced by an MCP route.

provider.description: Broker provider name (e.g. github). Validated against GET /providers at startup; Gate One never stores the provider's client secret.

header.description: Backend request header receiving the access token. Default Authorization. Host, Cookie, X-User-*, X-Forwarded-* and X-Gate-One-* names are refused.

prefix.description: Value prepended to the access token. Default "Bearer ". An explicit empty string sends the raw token.

browserCachePolicy.description: HTTP-cache orientation to the BROWSER for assets the origin serves with no Cache-Control (and no Last-Modified either: without these two headers the browser has no heuristic cache — every re-view re-fetches or revalidates each asset, one full round-trip each). Only 200 responses of content-type image/*, Cache-Control absent only: the origin's own declarations pass untouched. Sent as "private, max-age=…" — private: resources under authentication stay out of any shared cache; the origin's ETag remains for revalidation after expiry. Default: absent (headers preserved as-is).

imagesMaxAgeSeconds.description: Freshness duration (seconds) granted to the images (content-type image/*). E.g. 604800 = a week; 31536000 = a year (only if these files are immutable: the image names followed here are the capture timestamps, not content hashes — prefer a moderate duration if the app can re-edite a photo).

rewriteCookiesPolicy.description: Translation of the Set-Cookie set by the origin: a Domain attribute targeting its own namespace ("Domain=original…domain.dev") would be rejected by the browser from the public host — the cookie would be silently lost. Active: a Domain targeting the origin host (equal or parent) is rewritten to the public host in "rewrite" mode (the sharing scope — host + subdomains — is transposed as-is), or the attribute is removed in "strip" mode (host-only on the public host). Other cookies pass intact (surgery of the Domain attribute only: Path/Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite/Expires come out byte-exact). Auth protection: an origin Set-Cookie bearing a name reserved for the gateway session (access_token, refresh_token, id_token, session) is removed with a warning — set on the same public host, it would overwrite the session cookies. Default: absent (no cookie rewriting).

domain.description: "rewrite" (recommended) = Domain transposed to the public host; "strip" = Domain attribute removed.

rewriteBodyPolicy.description: Rewriting of the HTML body (200 text/html only, STREAMING — O(1) memory): the origin's absolute URLs cited in the pages ("https://origin/…", "http://origin/…", "//origin/…") are rewritten to the route's public host, so the browser stays in the proxy. Any explicit port is part of the rewritten prefix and is lost (target served on the standard port). The path, query and fragment follow as-is. Routes expanded from one wildcard automatically rewrite sibling editions toward their public hosts. `targets` and `followRoutes` add explicit cross-route mappings (bare hosts only: the request's scheme and port are inherited). At runtime (fetch/XHR/sendBeacon launched by the site), the client SW served on /__gate-one_pwa/sw.js applies the same policy — it is auto-registered by the guard script, served pre-authentication. One same policy (origins × exceptions × targets) is implemented three times (Go engine, client SW, script patch) — parity tested. Default: absent (no body rewriting).

enabled.description: true = engine active (the block is present to stay declarative; absent = disabled).

except.description: Exceptions by path prefix: string entry ("/reading/…") = these URLs stay at the ORIGIN (out-of-proxy reading link); object entry {path, to} = rewritten to an ALTERNATIVE public base. Longest prefix wins. '/…' prefix mandatory, '?'/'#' forbidden, 256 bytes max; 'to' = absolute http(s) URL, trailing slashes trimmed.

targets.description: Explicit cross-route mappings: backend origin host -> public route host. Bare hosts only (no scheme, port, path or wildcard); the key must be an origin of a declared route and the value the public host of a declared route. The request's scheme and port are inherited. Automatic wildcard siblings are added before these entries; a conflicting mapping is refused at load.

followRoutes.description: Selectors over declared routes BY PUBLIC HOST (exact host or '*.suffix'; a bare '*' is refused). Each selected route's backend origins are rewritten to its public host. Resolved after wildcard expansion; an unmatched selector, a self-only match or an ambiguous origin is refused at load.

oneOf.description: Path prefix kept at the origin (e.g. "/CorrespondancesBonPapaEtBonneMaman/" = origin-direct reading link).

host.description: Host of the route (routed by Host). Named capture {name}: one DNS label, expanded AT LOAD into one concrete route per allow-listed label of the wildcard block (bounded, fail-closed anti-SSRF).

wildcard.description: Named host/backend expansion — one route, N sites. Keys = capture names ({name} in host and backend), values = the ALLOW-LISTS of DNS labels they may take (a-z0-9, hyphens, no dots). The route expands at load into one concrete route per label; a label outside the lists has no route (fail-closed: the backend is never attacker-derived). With rewriteBody enabled, the expansion also compiles the cross-route map: an origin of another variant (e.g. es.wikipedia.org in the English edition) is rewritten to that sibling's public host; ambiguous alias mappings are left alone, and route-local except prefixes do not apply to siblings.

stripPrefix.description: Exact PUBLIC path prefix removed from the request before it reaches the backend. Path only (no query, fragment or wildcard), matched on segment boundaries and normalized at load (trailing slash removed; root "/" forbidden). Example: path "/api/*", stripPrefix "/api", backend "http://api:8080/v1" turns /api/foo into /v1/foo. The backend also receives X-Forwarded-Prefix when the ingress did not set one. Response paths are rewritten symmetrically: Location, Content-Location, Refresh/Link headers, Set-Cookie Path, and HTML URL attributes (href/src/action/srcset/poster, style url(), meta refresh) are brought back under /api; relative references and other origins are left untouched. Script strings and CSS @import are out of scope.

inject.description: Path of the route's custom injection bundle (JSON), relative to the config file. The bundle declares HTML/JS/CSS insertions by named target ("head" = after <head>/meta charset, "body-end" = before </body>) with per-page targeting (when = path prefix) and data-* attribute patches applied client-side by the guard. Inline content or file: (relative to the bundle, read at load — a faulty bundle refuses startup). Its formal grammar is inject-bundle.schema.json. See the doc's § upstream.inject.

frontend.description: Page route: auth failure → 302 to the login (API routes get a JSON 401); eligible for the guard script and the pwa policy.

autoHead.description: HEAD requests are served as GET, body removed.

uiGate.description: UI gating by config (CSS selectors) — embedded in the injected guard script. Only for non-modifiable fronts; an element's data-gtw-* markup wins over the rules.
